intro: Japanese keeps most verbs of change in pairs. The intransitive member says that a thing changes by itself: ドアが開く, the door opens. The transitive member says that someone changes it: ドアを開ける, I open the door. English often uses one verb for both (open, start, break), so you choose from the sentence: the thing with が and no doer means intransitive, the thing with を means transitive. And where English says 'was opened' or 'got broken', Japanese nearly always uses the intransitive, not the passive.

skills.rule: If the door or light simply changes, use the intransitive with が (開く, 閉まる, つく, 消える); if someone changes it, use the transitive with を (開ける, 閉める, つける, 消す).
skills.explain:
Four pairs: 開く (あく) / 開ける, 閉まる / 閉める, つく / つける, 消える / 消す. The intransitive describes the door or light changing: ドアが開く, 電気がつく. The transitive needs a doer and puts the thing in を: 窓を開ける, 電気をつける.

Japanese reports what happened to the thing even when a person was obviously involved: 'the shop opens at ten' is 店が十時に開く, 'the light went off' is 電気が消えた. English passives such as 'the door was closed' are the intransitive (閉まった), not 閉められた. Requests and offers are about doing it, so they take the transitive: 窓を開けてください.

Shape: -aru is intransitive and -eru transitive (閉まる / 閉める); a verb ending in -su is always transitive (消す). Careful: in 開く / 開ける and つく / つける the -eru verb is transitive, but in 消える / 消す it is the intransitive.

開く read あく is intransitive. Read ひらく it is a different verb that works both ways: 本を開く (open a book), 花が開く (a flower opens).
patterns: [thing] が 開く / 閉まる / つく / 消える
[person] が [thing] を 開ける / 閉める / つける / 消す
request: [thing] を 開けて / 閉めて / つけて / 消して ください

examples.jp: 窓[まど]を{開[あ]けて}ください。
examples.en: Please open the window.

examples.jp: ドアが{閉[し]まりました}。
examples.en: The door closed.

examples.jp: 部屋[へや]の電気[でんき]を{消[け]して}ください。
examples.en: Please turn off the light in the room.

examples.jp: このスーパーは朝[あさ]九時[くじ]に{開[あ]きます}。
examples.en: This supermarket opens at nine in the morning.

examples.jp: 暗[くら]いですね。電気[でんき]を{つけましょうか}。
examples.en: It's dark, isn't it? Shall I turn the light on?

examples.jp: 急[きゅう]にテレビが{消[き]えました}。
examples.en: The TV suddenly went off.

contrast.note: 'The window was opened' is 窓が開いた. The passive of the transitive is for something a person did that affected you, usually badly: 誰かに窓を開けられた.

contrast.vs: 開いている / 開けてある
contrast.note: Both describe a state now. 窓が開いている only says it is open; 窓が開けてある says someone opened it on purpose and left it so.
Same kanji, different verb: ひらく is both transitive (本を開く) and intransitive (花が開く). The door pair is あく / あける.

mistakes.note: With を you need the transitive. Or keep 開きました and change を to が.

mistakes.bad: 電気[でんき]が{消[け]しました}。
mistakes.good: 電気[でんき]が{消[き]えました}。
mistakes.note: A -su verb is always transitive. A light going off is 消えました.

mistakes.bad: テレビを{つきましょうか}。
mistakes.good: テレビを{つけましょうか}。
mistakes.note: An offer is something you do to the TV: transitive つける with を.

skills.tip: Ask 'who does it?' A doer in the sentence, or a request or offer: transitive with を. Only the thing: intransitive with が.

skills.rule: An event or machine that starts, ends, stops or goes on takes the intransitive with が (始まる, 終わる, 止まる, 続く); a person who does it takes the transitive with を (始める, 終える, 止める, 続ける).
skills.explain:
Events, schedules and machines are the subject of the intransitive: 授業が始まる, 会議が終わった, 電車が止まった, 雨が続いている. A person in control uses the transitive with を: 先生が授業を始める, 車を止める, 練習を続ける. Shape: -aru intransitive, -eru transitive (始まる / 始める, 止まる / 止める, 終わる / 終える); 続く / 続ける pairs -u with -eru.

終える sounds written or formal. In conversation 'finish something' is usually 終わらせる (宿題を終わらせた), and fixed announcements use 終わる with を (これで会議を終わります). But 'the film ended' is only 映画が終わった.

Boundaries. Rain, snow and noise stopping is 止む (やむ), not 止まる. Quitting a habit is やめる (タバコをやめる). After a verb stem, 'start to' and 'keep on' always take the -eru form, even with no object: 雨が降り始めた, 歩き続けた.
patterns: [event / machine] が 始まる / 終わる / 止まる / 続く
[person] が [thing] を 始める / 終える / 止める / 続ける
[verb stem] + 始める / 続ける (start to / keep on)

examples.jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]は九時[くじ]に{始[はじ]まります}。
examples.en: Class starts at nine.

examples.jp: では、テストを{始[はじ]めます}。
examples.en: Right, we will now begin the test.

examples.jp: 会議[かいぎ]は何時[なんじ]に{終[お]わりましたか}。
examples.en: What time did the meeting end?

examples.jp: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]で車[くるま]を{止[と]めて}ください。
examples.en: Please stop the car in front of the station.

examples.jp: 事故[じこ]で電車[でんしゃ]が{止[と]まりました}。
examples.en: The trains stopped because of an accident.

examples.jp: 暑[あつ]い日[ひ]が一週間[いっしゅうかん]{続[つづ]いて}います。
examples.en: The hot weather has gone on for a week.

contrast.note: Rain, snow, wind and noise stop by themselves with 止む: 雨が止んだ. 止まる is for vehicles, clocks and machines.
Giving up a habit or quitting an activity: タバコをやめた. 止める (とめる) is physically stopping something.
The everyday way to say you finished a task: 宿題を終わらせた. 終える means the same but sounds formal.

mistakes.bad: 映画[えいが]は九時[くじ]に{終[お]えました}。
mistakes.good: 映画[えいが]は九時[くじ]に{終[お]わりました}。
mistakes.note: The film does nothing to anything; it just ends.

mistakes.bad: 兄[あに]は大学[だいがく]で勉強[べんきょう]を{続[つづ]きました}。
mistakes.good: 兄[あに]は大学[だいがく]で勉強[べんきょう]を{続[つづ]けました}。
mistakes.note: A person keeps something going: transitive 続ける with を.

mistakes.bad: 雨[あめ]が{止[と]まりました}。
mistakes.good: 雨[あめ]が{止[や]みました}。
mistakes.note: Weather stops with 止む; 止まる is for cars, clocks and machines.

skills.tip: Is a person in charge of it? Yes: -eru with を (始める, 止める). No, it is an event or a machine: が with 始まる, 止まる, 続く.

skills.rule: When something moves in, out, up or down by itself, use the intransitive (入る, 出る, 上がる, 下がる, 落ちる); when someone moves it, use the transitive with を (入れる, 出す, 上げる, 下げる, 落とす).
skills.explain:
Ask what moves and whether it moves itself. 部屋に入る (I go in), but かばんに本を入れる (I put the book in). 家を出る (I go out), but ゴミを出す (I put the rubbish out). 値段が上がる, but 値段を上げる. 熱が下がった, but 音を下げる. りんごが落ちた, but 財布を落とした.

Shape: 上がる / 上げる and 下がる / 下げる are -aru / -eru; 入る / 入れる is -u / -eru; 出す and 落とす end in -su, and -su is always transitive.

The trap is を. With verbs of movement, を also marks the place you leave or pass through, so 家を出る, 部屋を出る, 階段を上がる are intransitive. Ask whether the を noun is a place you move through or a thing you move.

落とす is also the normal verb for losing something you dropped without noticing: 財布を落とした means 'I lost my wallet'. 財布が落ちた only reports the fall.
patterns: [person / thing] が [place] に 入る / [place] を 出る
[person] が [thing] を [place] に 入れる / [place] から 出す
[thing] が 上がる / 下がる / 落ちる
[person] が [thing] を 上げる / 下げる / 落とす

examples.jp: どうぞ、中[なか]に{入[はい]って}ください。
examples.en: Please come in.

examples.jp: コーヒーに砂糖[さとう]を{入[い]れますか}。
examples.en: Do you take sugar in your coffee?

examples.jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]七時[しちじ]に家[いえ]を{出[で]ます}。
examples.en: I leave home at seven every morning.

examples.jp: 月曜日[げつようび]にゴミを{出[だ]して}ください。
examples.en: Please put the rubbish out on Monday.

examples.jp: 薬[くすり]を飲[の]んで、熱[ねつ]が{下[さ]がりました}。
examples.en: I took some medicine and my fever went down.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]で財布[さいふ]を{落[お]として}しまいました。
examples.en: I lost my wallet at the station.

contrast.note: In 家を出る and 階段を上がる, を marks the place you leave or move along, not an object. The verb stays intransitive.
落ちる is a fall (an apple, a leaf; also failing an exam: 試験に落ちる). 下がる is going lower on a scale: prices, temperature, a fever.
Only for something done to you: 泥棒に入られた, 'we were burgled'. Something going in is 入る.

mistakes.bad: 来月[らいげつ]から電車[でんしゃ]の料金[りょうきん]が{上[あ]げます}。
mistakes.good: 来月[らいげつ]から電車[でんしゃ]の料金[りょうきん]が{上[あ]がります}。
mistakes.note: With が the fare itself goes up: intransitive. The company raises it: 会社が料金を上げる.

mistakes.bad: かばんに本[ほん]を{入[はい]りました}。
mistakes.good: かばんに本[ほん]を{入[い]れました}。
mistakes.note: You put the book in: transitive 入れる with を.

mistakes.bad: 手[て]を{上[あ]がって}ください。
mistakes.good: 手[て]を{上[あ]げて}ください。
mistakes.note: Raising your hand is something you do to it: 上げる.

skills.tip: Can you picture a hand moving the thing? Hand: transitive with を. No hand, the thing or person moves itself: intransitive. を before a place does not count.

skills.rule: Report damage or repair as a change in the thing with the intransitive (壊れる, 割れる, 切れる, 折れる, 直る, 汚れる); use the transitive with を when you name or own the doer (壊す, 割る, 切る, 折る, 直す, 汚す).
skills.explain:
Shape: five intransitives end in -reru. Three transitives just drop the -re-: 割れる / 割る, 切れる / 切る, 折れる / 折る. Two end in -su: 壊れる / 壊す, 汚れる / 汚す. 直る / 直す is -ru / -su. Every -su verb here is transitive.

The choice is about responsibility. パソコンが壊れた says the computer broke and blames nobody; パソコンを壊した says I broke it. A polite adult who dropped a plate owns it: お皿を割ってしまいました, すみません. Injuries to your own body also take the transitive: 足の骨を折った, though 骨が折れた is also fine.

Repair works the same way: 時計が直った (it works again), 父が時計を直した (father fixed it).

切れる has everyday uses: 電池が切れた (the battery ran out), 電話が切れた (the call cut off), 牛乳が切れている (we are out of milk). 切る is cutting with a blade or ending a call: 電話を切る.
patterns: [thing] が 壊れる / 割れる / 切れる / 折れる / 直る / 汚れる
[person] が [thing] を 壊す / 割る / 切る / 折る / 直す / 汚す
owning a mistake: [thing] を [transitive て] しまいました

examples.jp: パソコンが{壊[こわ]れました}。
examples.en: My computer broke.

examples.jp: 弟[おとうと]がおもちゃを{壊[こわ]しました}。
examples.en: My younger brother broke the toy.

examples.jp: 携帯[けいたい]の電池[でんち]が{切[き]れました}。
examples.en: My phone battery has run out.

examples.jp: すみません、お皿[さら]を{割[わ]って}しまいました。
examples.en: I'm sorry, I've broken a plate.

examples.jp: 自転車[じてんしゃ]はもう{直[なお]りましたか}。
examples.en: Is the bicycle fixed yet?

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]の中[なか]を歩[ある]いて、靴[くつ]が{汚[よご]れました}。
examples.en: My shoes got dirty walking in the rain.

contrast.vs: 割れる / 壊れる / 折れる
contrast.note: 割れる: breaks into pieces (glass, plates, eggs). 壊れる: a machine or structure stops working or falls apart. 折れる: a long thing snaps (a bone, a pencil, a branch).
Only for damage someone did to you: 弟にゲームを壊された. The neutral report is 壊れた.
Same readings, different kanji: illness and injuries heal with 治る. 直る is for objects and mistakes.

mistakes.bad: 足[あし]の骨[ほね]が{折[お]りました}。
mistakes.good: 足[あし]の骨[ほね]が{折[お]れました}。
mistakes.note: With が the bone is the subject: intransitive 折れる. 足の骨を折りました is also correct.

mistakes.bad: 店[みせ]の人[ひと]が時計[とけい]を{直[なお]りました}。
mistakes.good: 店[みせ]の人[ひと]が時計[とけい]を{直[なお]しました}。
mistakes.note: The shop assistant did the repair: transitive 直す with を.

mistakes.bad: コーヒーで服[ふく]を{汚[よご]れて}しまいました。
mistakes.good: コーヒーで服[ふく]を{汚[よご]して}しまいました。
mistakes.note: With を you are the doer: 汚す. Or say 服が汚れてしまいました.

skills.tip: Reporting, or keeping blame out: が with the -reru verb (割れた). Naming or owning the doer: を with the transitive (割ってしまった).
